extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy of science and physics; general educated readers interested in foundations of mechanics
extracted.subtask_description: Close-reading of a philosophical/educational chapter discussing the concepts of indestructibility of matter, continuity of motion, and persistence (conservation) of force, with illustrative examples and epistemological caveats. Useful for analyzing conceptual foundations and justificatory standards in physical science.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indestructibility of Matter (as persistence of force)
rubrics_metrics.description: By the Indestructibility of Matter we really mean the indestructibility of the force with which Matter affects us.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evidence for indestructibility is always in terms of the constancy of the force a quantity of matter exerts (e.g., gravitative force measured by scales, chemical force inferred from neutralization). When a substance becomes invisible (gas) but its total gravitative force is unchanged, we infer the matter still exists. The proper interpretation is that permanence of matter is shown by permanence of its resisting/affecting force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuity of Motion (as continuity of force/principle of activity)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Continuity of Motion is the continuity, not of visible translation through space, but of that something (a principle of activity or force) which has motion for one of its sensible forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apparent cessations of translation (e.g., pendulum at turning points) are accompanied by latent forms (strain, molecular motion) so that 'perceptible activity plus latent activity yield a constant sum.' Examples: pendulum oscillations, ball on an elastic string, planetary orbits (average speed constant despite local accelerations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Motion's translation is a sign, not the continuous existence
rubrics_metrics.description: Translation through space is not itself an existence but a manifestation (a sign) of an existence; cessation of translation does not imply cessation of the underlying existence (principle of activity).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To correctly assert continuity one must identify what persists: the principle of activity which may appear as translation at some times and as strain or latent activity at others. The text uses the chandelier, pendulum, and elastic-string examples to show how visible motion alternates with latent strain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of activity identified with Force and muscular effort
rubrics_metrics.description: The principle of activity that persists is ultimately conceived by us in terms of Force, and psychologically is the objective correlative of our subjective sense of muscular effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vision alone gives no idea of the principle of activity; visible motion suggests by association a principle appreciable by touch and muscles. Thus continuity of Motion and indestructibility of Matter are known to us in terms of Force.

rubrics_metrics.name: All proofs of continuity/indestructibility presuppose constancy of force
rubrics_metrics.description: All proofs of the Continuity of Motion and Indestructibility of Matter involve the postulate that the quantity of force is constant (i.e., action and reaction equal and opposite).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Astronomical inferences (planetary identity, orbital calculations) and laboratory measurements rely on laws of force which embody the axiom that force cannot be destroyed. The inference that motion is indestructible depends on accounting for motion communicated to or received from other bodies according to force-laws.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measurement presupposes persistence of units (and so cannot prove persistence of force)
rubrics_metrics.description: Quantitative science and measurement presuppose fixed units of linear extension and of force; persistence of force cannot be proved by measurements that tacitly assume that persistence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Units of length (standards) and derived units of weight/gravitative force are assumed constant in experiments (e.g., chemist's scales used to show mass conservation). If units vary, conclusions about indestructibility fail. Thus attempts to establish persistence by measurement beg the question by taking persistence as given.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction between intrinsic (space-occupying) force and extrinsic force (energy)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two fundamentally-different classes of force must be distinguished: (1) the force by which matter demonstrates itself as occupying space (intrinsic, passive) and (2) the force by which it demonstrates itself as acting (extrinsic, active — called Energy).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Intrinsic force is resistance to effort (what makes body distinct from space). Extrinsic force includes actual and potential energy (molar motion, heat, light). In aggregated matter these modes intermix (e.g., chemical potential plus heat). Psychological awareness (sense of effort) is the common subjective symbol for both.

rubrics_metrics.name: Energy as the active (extrinsic) form of force — actual and potential
rubrics_metrics.description: Energy is the name for the mode of force that causes or will cause change; what was called perceptible activity is actual energy, and latent activity is potential energy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Energy includes the power shown in movements of masses and molecules; transformations among molar motion, heat, light are encompassed. The text emphasizes that energy is extrinsic and dependent on relations among bodies, unlike intrinsic space-occupying force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conceive latent activity as strain in medium (heuristic for continuity)
rubrics_metrics.description: To account for disappearance of perceptible motion (e.g., a body projected up and stopped by gravity), we must conceive the principle of activity as becoming latent in the strain between the body and Earth or in the medium occupying space.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations: elastic string attached to a ball (strain stores activity), imaginary series of strings to simulate gravitative action. Without conceiving latent activity in the medium, one would have to conceive power turning into a space-relation, which is inconceivable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terminology recommendation: prefer 'persistence' over 'conservation' of force
rubrics_metrics.description: The author prefers the term 'persistence' of force to 'conservation' because 'conservation' implies a conserver and an act of conserving and tacitly assumes pre-existence of the force.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is partly a philosophical/terminological caution. 'Persistence' avoids suggesting an external conserver and better fits the intended conception that force's continued presence need not imply an agent that conserves it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Caveat about purely physical formulations that ignore consciousness of Force
rubrics_metrics.description: Formulating phenomena solely in terms of body, space, and motion while discharging from concepts the consciousness of Force loses the foundation of physical conceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Physicists' definitions (e.g., potential energy as spatial relations 'in themselves nothing') suffice for physical inquiry but not for philosophical purposes; psychological origins of concepts (muscular tension as ultimate symbol) matter for philosophical analysis.
